tutorial: No tutorial: the 16 Workshop tools (Make: mass_calibrate, slice_open, printer_*; SafetyNet: macro_*, pref_history, pref_rollback, app_recover) that no model had proven. One small box, a test macro, a test settings key and a dummy printer on the Mac's own loopback address.

conventions.run: Agent Link for FreeCAD's batch, in order; { $from, $at } takes a value from an earlier call's answer (agentlink/chain.py). REFUSED in expect means the call must answer an error with that code.
conventions.printers: Every printer_* call names the dummy printer (alink-hardening-dummy, http://127.0.0.1:9, kind moonraker, no key) so that a printer the person keeps is never the one a call falls to. The only network traffic is call 36: one request to 127.0.0.1 port 9, refused by the Mac itself. pause, stop and start are never sent with their confirm.
conventions.settings: pref_rollback is only called with a `to` that has no snapshot. Calls 27 and 29 set and remove the test-only key Mod/AgentLink/LiveTest/Probe so that pref_history has a known newest row; leave those two calls and call 28 out if no settings write at all is wanted (pref_history is then proven by call 26 alone).
conventions.leftBehind: the macro file alink-hardening-probe.FCMacro in FreeCAD's macro folder (no tool deletes a macro; it is not approved, so Agent Link will not run it); one checkpoint of WorkshopRest; alink-probe-box.step in the session's folder. No printer, no setting.

notCovered: macro_approve accepted and macro_run running the macro: the approval is the person's typed words (macro_approve's description: confirm "approve <name>" typed by them, never by the agent). When the person types `approve alink-hardening-probe` in chat, run: macro_show { name } for them to read, macro_approve { name: "alink-hardening-probe", confirm: "approve alink-hardening-probe" } (expect approved, sha256), doc_new { name: "MacroRun" }, macro_run { name: "alink-hardening-probe", params: { LENGTH: 60 } } (expect ran, calls 1, params, bodies ['Probe box'] with box [60, 20, 10], checkpoint), macro_run { name, params: { WIDTH: 5 } } (REFUSED invalid_input: WIDTH not among the named sizes (LENGTH)), then macro_unapprove { name } (was true) and macro_run again (REFUSED not_allowed).

pref_rollback putting settings back: it writes the whole settings file and restarts FreeCAD, and it has no dry form (only `to` and `save`). A safe proof needs a throwaway FreeCAD profile (a second user config folder), not the person's: pref_set a test key, pref_history, pref_rollback { to: that change }, then pref_get shows the key gone after the restart.

slice_open opening a project: it starts OrcaSlicer's own window in front of the person and has no quiet form (its slicer enum is orcaslicer | bambustudio, so there is no 'not installed' road to read on a Mac that has OrcaSlicer). A proof needs the person at the Mac and their word: slice_with { body, slicer: "orcaslicer", project: true, name: "probe-orca" } on a body in a print setup, then slice_open { path: "probe-orca.3mf" } (expect opened, in 'orcaslicer', next naming slice_read).

printer_status answering a state, printer_send uploading, printer_pause / printer_stop accepted: each needs a real printer (or a stand-in server speaking Moonraker's API on the Mac) and, for start, pause and stop, the person's own confirm. Without one, only the refusals above can be run. A safe proof: a local Moonraker stand-in on 127.0.0.1 (the repository's tests/make/test_printer.py runs one), kept under a dummy name, with no printer behind it.
printer_send with a real .gcode to the dummy (REFUSED unavailable after the file checks): needs a G-code file, which only a slicer writes; slice or slice_with first when one is wanted.
app_recover auto and accept: they open recovered copies and save over the person's file; only list and the two refusals are run here (the task asks for the read-only use).
mass_calibrate with a print setup (key setup:S1) and with encased parts: workshop-make-model.json builds those; here the body is in no setup on purpose, so the key is solid:pla.
